title: M&A Auto Service: choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Trade Counter. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Three more challengers wait in the re-roll pool (a defaced club sleeve, cephalopod skin, and a pastel mascot sheet), none of which can carry a Bristol garage's trust job.

options.label: The Trade Counter
options.lineage: British motor factor parts counter: shelf-edge labels, dockets, stock boards
options.thesis: The industrial estate's own retail language, turned on the garage itself: high-vis amber, black keylines, and one docket that hands you the number.
options.viewport: Full-bleed amber. M&A AUTO SERVICE set as a heavy shelf-edge header in black condensed caps, then a torn-edge counter docket carrying 07882 209735 at ticket scale as the primary tap, with 4.8 / 102 stamped beside it like a stock rating.
options.risk: Catalogue grammar could imply they sell parts. Mitigated by carrying only real services and real numbers in the rows, never a price or a part code.
options.case: Wins both axes. A north Bristol driver knows the amber-and-black trade counter by heart, and it is honest about being a working unit on an estate rather than a forecourt.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscope on a signal bench
options.thesis: The trace snapping out of noise and locking still: diagnosis as the whole visual argument.
options.viewport: Near-black glass, a green trace riding a ten-division grid, the phone number set as an armed amber readout.
options.risk: Green-on-black electronics lab reads as tech, not garage, and buries the one thing that matters.
options.case: Fuses on meaning, since 'diagnosed the issue quickly' is literally this, but loses audience identification badly: a driver with a dead battery does not see themselves in a lab instrument.

options.label: Build Instructions
options.thesis: Wordless exploded steps: taken apart, understood, put back exactly right.
options.viewport: Sky-blue page, oversized step numerals, an exploded call-out with arrows seating each piece.
options.risk: Toy-instruction sky blue reads playful, which is the wrong register for a trust decision made in a hurry.
options.case: The exploded-diagram grammar is real automotive DNA (it is Haynes-manual lineage), but the toy framing costs the trust this page exists to win.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.lineage: early one-bit desktop, dithered grays and pixel chrome
options.thesis: Everything in overlapping windows, every tone a stipple dither, nothing but black and white pixels.
options.viewport: A white desktop plane with a titled window holding the garage's details in pixel caps.
options.risk: A retro-computing joke on a page whose job is to make a stranger trust a mechanic.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it is a coherent interface language, but nothing in it belongs to a Bristol driver's world, and one-bit dither cannot carry a 4.8-star reputation.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The independent-garage site done properly: dark graphite, one confident accent, big type, phone number pinned, reviews stacked.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects, at full craft and no irony.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other garage site, which is the point of taking it.
